Truth is Not a Minted Coin
The Dogmatic View
The Hegelian View
Truth and falsehood are seen as fixed, isolated
essences, like a stamped coin ready for one's pocket.
In this view, falsehood is simply discarded like slag.
The false is not a demon to be banished; it is the
negative of substance. Inequality and failure are
the essential, active moments of differentiation.
The shapes of spirit that fail are necessary. The truth is a bacchanalian revel
where not a member is sober, because, in isolating himself from the revel, each
member is just as immediately dissolved into it.

The Truth of Self-Certainty: The Recognition Loop
Subject A
(Master)
The Demand: Self-consciousness exists
only when recognized by another. Subject
A asserts authority and subjugates
Subject B to force recognition.
The Contradiction
By reducing Subject B to a slave, Subject
B's recognition becomes worthless. The
Master's certainty is trapped in a dead end.
Subiect B
(Slave)
The Sublation: The Slave, forced into labor
and fear of death, works upon the material
world. Through this objective labor, the
Slave achieves a fully developed, actualized
self-consciousness that the Master lacks.

From Observation to Actualization
Observing Reason
Purposive Doing
The attempt to find the essence of mind in
static, physical correlations. It treats human
activity from the 'outside' as a physical event,
inevitably failing to capture life.
Hegel rejects the 'inner psychological state
causing an outer movement' model. Rational
agents start with purposes and actualize
them through work. Reason is an active,
developmental doing.

The Premise
We begin with the most banal,
obvious assumption possible.
The Claim
We are absolutely certain that we
are aware of worldly items right
'Here' and right 'Now'.
The Method
We will not bring outside theories
to this claim. We will simply test if
this certainty holds up to its own
expression.

The Anatomy of a "Now"
To the question: "What is the Now?"
we answer: "The Now is midday." We
write this truth down. A truth cannot
be lost by being written down.
If now, this night, we look at this
truth which has been written down,
we will have to say that it has
become rather stale.
The 'Now' maintains itself, but as a negative (it is not day, it
is not night). The immediate 'Now' has vanished
